gloss: to get nervous; to get stage fright

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: あがっていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to get nervous; to get stage fright; to freeze up
definitions.explanation: To become extremely nervous or tense in front of others, especially when speaking publicly, performing, or facing an important situation. The anxiety causes one to lose composure or forget what to say.

examples.japanese: ⟦{人前|ひとまえ}→人前：19380_hitomae⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧あがってしまう。
examples.english: I get nervous in front of people.

examples.japanese: ⟦{面接|めんせつ}→面接：01100_mensetsu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧あがって、⟦うまく→うまい：01279_umai⟧⟦{話|はな}せなかった→話す：00467_hanasu⟧。
examples.english: I got nervous during the interview and couldn't speak well.

examples.japanese: ⟦{初|はじ}めて→初めて：02932_hajimete⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{舞台|ぶたい}→舞台：03606_butai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦すっかり→すっかり：01270_sukkari⟧あがってしまい、セリフ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{忘|わす}れた→忘れる：00474_wasureru⟧。
examples.english: I completely froze up on my first stage performance and forgot my lines.

notes:
USAGE:
This あがる is distinct from ⟦{上|あ}がる→上がる：00615_agaru⟧ (to go up, to rise). When used to mean "get nervous," it is typically written in hiragana. The metaphor comes from blood "rising" to one's head, causing flushing and mental confusion.

Common patterns include ⟦あがり{症|しょう}→あがり症：21562_agarishou⟧ (tendency to get nervous, stage fright as a condition) and あがってしまう (to end up freezing from nerves). Often used with ⟦{人前|ひとまえ}→人前：19380_hitomae⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧ (in front of people) or ⟦{本番|ほんばん}→本番：19392_honban⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧ (at the actual performance).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{人前|ひとまえ}→人前：19380_hitomae⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧あがる (to get nervous in front of people)
- ⟦あがり{症|しょう}→あがり症：21562_agarishou⟧ (stage fright, nervousness as a trait)
- ⟦すっかり→すっかり：01270_sukkari⟧あがる (to completely freeze up)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{緊張|きんちょう}する→緊張する：20557_kinchousuru⟧: to be tense, nervous — more general term; あがる specifically implies losing composure or being unable to function
